It's a prescribed medication, so the doctor has determined that it's necessary for the person's health. From a medical standpoint, carrying it would be the responsible thing to do because it can save a life in an emergency. Now, from a Christian viewpoint, I think about the principles of stewardship and care for the body. The Bible teaches that our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19-20), so taking care of our health is important. Using prescribed medication, like an EpiPen, would be part of that stewardship. It's not about relying on medicine instead of God, but using the resources God has provided through medical knowledge. I also consider the principle of neighbor love. If someone has a severe allergy, carrying an EpiPen can prevent a life-threatening situation. Romans 13:1 says to be subject to the authorities, which can extend to medical professionals in matters of health. I should also think about any potential concerns.
